title: Affine-Image Propagation for Tight and Scalable Neural Network Verification
claim: Prior bounds lose tightness by enclosing the domain in coarse shapes and fixing the slope; ours keeps the exact set and optimizes the slope.
layout: 4 panels in a row, left-to-right, shared legends under each, geometric then functional
description: Four side-by-side 2-D sketches with bold titles. Panels (a) and (b) are labeled 'Geometric loss'. In (a), a salmon-colored tilted ellipse, the affine image, sits inside a large light-blue box (α-CROWN) on z1/z2 axes, with a dot marking the center ẑ. In (b), the same ellipse sits inside a green box-intersect-ellipsoid shape (prior SDP-CROWN) with clipped corners. Panels (c) and (d) are labeled 'Functional loss'. Each plots y against z with a blue triangular α-CROWN feasible region and a salmon curved SDP-CROWN region under it. In (c) a blue sloped line is labeled g(α)ᵀz+h(α,λ). In (d) a flat salmon line is labeled gᵀz+h(g,λ) and touches the top of the region. Legends sit below each pair. Salmon marks 'ours' throughout.
caption: Geometric and functional loss in bound propagation. (a) $\alpha$-CROWN incurs geometric loss by enclosing the affine image in a box. (b) Prior SDP-CROWN reduces this loss by intersecting the box with an axis-aligned ellipsoid. Our method retains the affine image, avoiding this source of geometric loss. (c) In this example, the linear upper bound with inherited slope $g(\alpha)=\zub/(\zub-\zlb)$ cannot be tightened even though SDP-CROWN has a smaller feasible region. (d) We allow the slope $g$ to be optimized, allowing it to exploit the smaller feasible region.
abstract: While bound propagation methods are highly effective for certifying neural networks against $\ell_{\infty}$ adversaries, tight and scalable verification for $\ell_{2}$ adversaries remains a significant open challenge. Existing methods incur geometric loss by enclosing preactivation sets in elementwise intervals or axis-aligned ellipsoids, and functional loss by restricting the linear bounds constructed over those domains. Consequently, tight $\ell_{2}$ verification is currently restricted to Lipschitz-regularized networks where these approximations are accurate. In this paper, we introduce affine-image SDP-CROWN, a novel bound propagation method that better approximates preactivation domains using affine-image constraints and jointly optimizes the linear bound to adapt to the resulting domain. To bypass the prohibitive computational cost of dense semidefinite constraints required by the affine-image representation, we replace them with scaled diagonal-dominance conditions, allowing a GPU-accelerated implementation. Our method preserves the bound propagation recursion and can be integrated with branch-and-bound. On five MNIST and CIFAR-10 non-Lipschitz-regularized networks, our method improves verified accuracy over state-of-the-art methods by 17% to 57.5%. With branch-and-bound, these improvements increase to between 27% and 63.5%.
